title: 'Search Only in this folder' gives wrong or missing results when the folder's path has a space or bracket (names and contents)
problem: A folder-scoped search is narrowed inside fff by gluing a `rel/**` glob onto the query text, which breaks for ordinary folder names. Name search (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:623-635) builds the glob only when the folder's path inside the root has no whitespace and none of `*?[]{}!` or backslash; otherwise (665-669) it asks fff for the root-wide top 20,000 matches and keeps those under the folder by prefix (682-688). In a large root (docs/manual.md:368 quotes about 310,000 files in a home folder) a short query's in-folder matches need not be among the root-wide top 20,000, so they go missing with no sign, and every keystroke builds 20,000 paths. Content search (Engine::grep, 899-905, appended to the pattern at 935) fares worse. (1) Any whitespace in the path ('Documents/Tax Returns', 'Google Drive/My Drive', 'Application Support') drops the glob at line 904, so the whole root is grepped with page_limit = limit (912) and hits are filtered afterwards (970-974). fff orders files by frecency then newest (fff-search grep/prefilter.rs:171-175), so the page fills with out-of-scope matches and the folder shows few or no results; files_with_matches/files_searched (963-964) count the wrong files and the time limit is spent outside the folder. (2) Only whitespace is screened there, so a scope such as `app/[slug]` or `photos[2024]` becomes a character-class glob (GrepConfig treats any wildcard token containing '/' as a glob, fff-query-parser config.rs:124) that does not match the folder: nothing is found. (3) Because the glob makes query.constraints non-empty, fff's literal fallback (fff-search grep/grep.rs:217-267) fires whenever the scoped search finds nothing: it re-greps every file of the root for the literal string `<query> <rel>/**`, keeping only FilePath constraints. With content_index off (default) that reads the whole location until time_limit_secs (5 s default, unbounded when None), so a no-hit search in a small folder spins for the full time limit, and text like `a != b` (swallowed as an exclusion) is never retried inside the folder.
proposal: Stop encoding the scope as query text. Content search (Engine::grep): parse only the user's pattern with QueryParser::new(GrepConfig), then add the scope programmatically with `query.constraints.push(Constraint::PathSegment(&rel))` (rel = '/'-separated path inside the base; PathSegment matches a multi-segment prefix case-insensitively with no glob metacharacters or tokenisation, fff-search index/constraints.rs:91-123, 337-340) and keep the exact `path.starts_with(scope)` post-filter. In the multi-pattern branch push the same constraint into `constraints` instead of appending to pattern 0 (941-948). For scoped searches set `query.raw_query` to the empty string so fff's whole-root literal fallback is skipped (grep.rs:227-230; grep_text() does not use raw_query when fuzzy_query is non-empty), and do the retry in the engine, still inside the scope: if the result is empty, next_file_offset == 0 and the user's text produced constraints (or an Empty fuzzy query), call picker.grep again with an FFFQuery whose raw_query is empty, whose constraints hold only the scope, and whose fuzzy_query is FuzzyQuery::Text(text.trim()). FFFQuery, FuzzyQuery and Constraint are re-exported by fff_search. Name search (search_root, replacing 629-635): give it the same constraint, or, where a programmatic constraint does not fit, a shared helper `fn scope_glob(rel: &str) -> String` that replaces each run of characters a token cannot carry literally (whitespace, `* ? [ ] { } !`, backslash) with a single `*` and appends `/**`, so `Tax Returns [2024]` becomes `Tax*Returns*2024*/**`; fff's default glob backend is globset (fff-search-0.11.0/Cargo.toml:29, default = [ripgrep]; src/index/constraints.rs:517-520), where `*` matches any run of characters, so the glob is a superset of the folder and the exact starts_with check at 684 keeps results precise. With the scope always narrowed inside fff, remove the `scope_rel.is_some() && scope_glob.is_none()` 20,000 over-fetch arm at 665. Add a CHANGELOG entry.
original_test_plan: Unit tests in engine.rs (style of search_settings_change_content_search). Temp root with `My Notes/a.txt`, `My Docs [old]/needle.txt` and `app/[slug]/page.txt` containing `needle`, plus about 50 `other/f{i}.txt` decoys containing `needle` and `d/needle-N.txt` name decoys; set the in-scope files' mtime an hour back with File::set_modified so they sort last. Grep with scope `My Notes` and limit 10 returns exactly a.txt (today 0 hits, the page fills from other/); scope `app/[slug]` returns page.txt and scope `photos[2024]`-style folders return their file (today 0). Add a line `a != b` to a.txt and assert a scoped grep for it finds it. A scoped grep for an absent word returns no hits and files_searched <= the files in the scope. Name search `needle` scoped to `My Docs [old]`: hits == [needle.txt] and total_matched == 1 (today it counts the decoys). If the helper is used: scope_glob of `Tax Returns [2024]` == `Tax*Returns*2024*/**` and of `a/b` == `a/b/**`. Headless UI test in tests/controls.rs: create `My Notes/` in the Fixture before Ui::open, go_to it, click `scope-folder` and `by-contents`, set_query, assert ui.names().
original_risks: Relies on fff-search 0.11.0 behaviour (an empty raw_query disables its literal fallback); pin it with a unit test. PathSegment is a superset match (same folder path elsewhere in the tree, case-insensitive), as is the `*` glob, so the exact post-filter must stay. For the glob helper: a relative path made only of special characters turns into `*/**`, which is no narrower than today; if the project ever switches fff-search to its zlob feature `*` stops crossing '/', which is still correct because the replaced characters are never '/'. The name half and the content half can be split.

verifier.claim_check:
The problem is real; I read the code only (no cargo run). Three details of the candidate are wrong or need correcting.

CONFIRMED (content search)
- crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:899-905 builds the scope as query text ` {rel}/**` and drops it when rel has any whitespace (line 904). With no glob, the single-pattern branch (935-936) greps the whole root with page_limit = limit (912); hits are prefix-filtered only afterwards (970-974).
- fff sorts candidates by frecency then mtime (fff-search-0.11.0/src/grep/prefilter.rs:171-175) and stops when the page fills (grep/grep.rs:672-678). Engine::grep never follows next_file_offset, so in-scope hits are silently lost once the root has `limit` earlier matches. The UI asks for limit = result_limit*4 = 2000 lines, per_file 20 (src/finder/mod.rs:2999-3006).
- The 5 s budget (time_budget_ms, enforce_time_budget at 924-927) is spent reading the whole root, and files_with_matches (963) counts out-of-scope files; the UI shows that as total_matched (src/finder/mod.rs:3023).
- Only whitespace is screened in grep, so `app/[slug]/**` is parsed as a Glob (fff-query-parser-0.11.0/src/config.rs GrepConfig::is_glob_pattern: any wildcard token containing '/'). globset compiles `[slug]` as a character class, so no file matches. Name search does screen `*?[]{}!\` (629-635).
- Literal fallback: grep/grep.rs:222-267 re-greps every file for the raw string `<query> <rel>/**` whenever a constrained search is a full-scan miss, keeping only FilePath constraints. The scope glob is itself a constraint, so every no-hit scoped search (ordinary folder names included) triggers a root-wide pass, up to the time limit when content_index is off (the default). The engine passes no abort signal, so stale keystroke searches keep running.

CONFIRMED (name search)
- engine.rs:665 over-fetches 20,000 root-wide for special-character scopes and filters by prefix (682-688). total_matched is then root-wide, and matches beyond the top 20,000 are lost; that needs a large root and a common query, so it is real but narrower than the content case.

WRONG OR NEEDS CORRECTING
1. `a != b` is not swallowed in fff-query-parser 0.11.0: parser.rs parse_negation keeps a negated token with fewer than 3 inner characters as text. The real casualty is different. Gluing the glob on makes a lone constraint-like pattern (`src/`, `*.rs`, `!important`, `type:x`) a two-token query, so fuzzy_query is Empty and extract_grep_text (grep.rs:499-514) greps the literal `src/ rel/**`. Such scoped content searches return nothing, while the same search unscoped works.
2. PathSegment is a superset match (constraints.rs:91-123: any `/seg/` anywhere, ASCII case-insensitive). Using it for every scope would make currently exact scopes inexact: a top-level `src`, `docs` or `Documents` would also pull in every nested folder of that name, bringing back page and fetch crowding and inflating the counts. Today's anchored `rel/**` glob has neither problem.
3. The proposed `files_searched <= files in scope` assertion does not pin the fallback: when the fallback finds nothing, fff returns the first pass's result (grep.rs:262-263), so that assertion passes today.

OTHER CHECKS
- Not already handled: content_search (src/finder/mod.rs:2993) and src/server/mod.rs:477 call engine.grep directly.
- Not documented as intended in docs/manual.md (326-335) or CHANGELOG.md.
- No test pins the current behaviour: engine.rs searches_a_folder and tests/controls.rs search_scope_button only use plain folder names.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Stop encoding the scope as query text, as proposed, but push an anchored, escaped Glob constraint instead of PathSegment. It keeps today's exact semantics for ordinary folders and fixes the special ones.

1. Shared helper in engine.rs
- `fn scope_glob(rel: &str) -> String`: wrap each of `? * [ ] { }` and `\` in brackets (`[[]`, `[]]`, `[*]`, `[\]`), copy everything else (spaces, `!`, commas) unchanged, then append `/**`.
- This mirrors globset::escape (globset-0.4.21/src/lib.rs:1133). Do not emit `[!]`; `!` only negates inside a class and that form is an unclosed class.
- A backslash inside a class is literal on every platform (glob.rs parse_class has no escape handling). The compiled regex is anchored `^…$` and case-sensitive, and the constraint string goes straight to globset::Glob::new (fff-search index/constraints.rs:517-520), so no tokenisation happens.
- Add `Constraint, FFFQuery, FuzzyQuery` to the `use fff_search::{…}` list; they are re-exported through `pub use fff_query_parser::*`. FFFQuery's fields are public, and fff builds one by hand itself in file_picker.rs:1375-1380.

2. Engine::grep (899-959)
- Compute `scope_glob: Option<String>` from rel without the whitespace filter and without the leading space.
- Single pattern, no scope: unchanged, `picker.grep(&parser.parse(only), &options)`.
- Single pattern, scoped:
  - `let mut q = parser.parse(only); let user_constrained = !q.constraints.is_empty(); q.constraints.push(Constraint::Glob(glob)); q.raw_query = "";`
  - The empty raw_query disables fff's root-wide literal fallback (grep.rs:227-230). raw_query is otherwise read only when fuzzy_query is Empty (grep.rs:499-514).
  - Run `picker.grep(&q, &options)`; skip this pass when q.fuzzy_query is Empty, since the grep text would be empty.
  - If that pass was skipped, or it returned no matches with next_file_offset == 0 and user_constrained, retry inside the scope: `picker.grep(&FFFQuery { raw_query: "", constraints: vec![Constraint::Glob(glob)], fuzzy_query: FuzzyQuery::Text(only.trim()), location: None }, &options)`.
  - Give the retry only the remaining time (clone options with time_budget_ms reduced by started.elapsed() when time_limit_secs > 0) so two passes cannot run to twice the limit.
- Multi-pattern branch: parse each pattern unmodified and push `Constraint::Glob(glob)` into `constraints` instead of appending to pattern 0. multi_grep has no literal fallback (multi_pattern.rs:124).
- Keep the starts_with post-filter (970-974) and the stopped/files_* bookkeeping.

3. search_root (623-669)
- Build the glob with the same helper for every scope_rel and drop the character filter at 631-634.
- Do not append it to `query` (delete 649-652). After each of the three `QueryParser::…parse(&query)` calls (697, 712, 740), make the parsed query mutable and push `Constraint::Glob(glob)`. All three paths apply query.constraints through apply_constraints (score.rs:403, 611), for directories as well as files.
- Remove the `scope_rel.is_some() && scope_glob.is_none()` arm at 665.
- Keep the scope glob out of fold_glob_case; it must stay case-sensitive.

4. Side effects to accept and name in the PR
- raw_query no longer carries the scope. The query-tracker lookup key (file_picker.rs:1121) then equals what track_open records (engine.rs:1312), so combo boost starts working in scoped Any-kind searches.
- A lone `dir/` query in a scoped mixed search becomes folders-only (file_picker.rs:1261), as it already is unscoped.
- Lone constraint-like tokens are parsed the same scoped and unscoped.

5. CHANGELOG.md: add a `### Fixed` section under [Unreleased]. docs/manual.md needs no change.

Pitfalls
- rel comes from to_string_lossy with `\` replaced by `/`; keep that.
- Do not use the lossy `Tax*Returns*2024*/**` helper from the proposal; a pushed constraint needs no tokenisation.
- PathSegment is an acceptable fallback only if kept for special-character scopes; never use it for all scopes.
verifier.test_plan:
Unit tests in the `mod tests` of crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs, in the style of `searches_a_folder` and `search_settings_change_content_search`: a temp dir under std::env::temp_dir() with the pid in its name, `Engine::new(EngineOptions { roots: vec![dir], app_dirs: vec![], db_dir: None, watch: false, search: Default::default() })`, `engine.wait_ready(Duration::from_secs(10))`, then `engine.grep(&GrepRequest { .. })` / `engine.search(&SearchRequest { .. })` and `display_name`. All files must exist, with mtimes set, before Engine::new.

1. Whitespace scope crowding: `My Notes/a.txt` containing `needle`, mtime set an hour back with `File::set_modified`, plus 50 `other/f{i}.txt` containing `needle`. Grep scope `My Notes`, limit 10: hits == [a.txt] and files_with_matches == 1. Today this gives 0 hits because the page fills from other/.
2. Glob characters: `app/[slug]/page.txt`, `photos[2024]/p.txt`, `x{a,b}/f.txt`, each containing `needle`; a scoped grep returns exactly that file (0 today). Under `#[cfg(unix)]` add `q*r?/f.txt` and a folder name with a backslash.
3. Fallback pin (replaces the proposal's files_searched assertion): `plain/empty.txt` without the word, and `other/trap.txt` containing the line `zzz plain/**`. Grep `zzz` scoped to `plain`: hits are empty and files_with_matches == 0. Today it is 1, because fff's root-wide literal fallback finds the trap. This guards the empty-raw_query behaviour against fff upgrades.
4. Constraint-like patterns in scope: `plain/style.css` with the lines `color: red !important` and `see src/ and *.rs`. Scoped greps for `!important`, `src/` and `*.rs` each return one hit (all 0 today). `a != b` can be a sanity check only; it already works.
5. Multi-pattern: patterns ["needle", "zzz"] scoped to `My Notes` return only a.txt.
6. Name search: `My Docs [old]/needle.txt` plus 30 `d/needle-{i}.txt`. Search `needle` scoped to `My Docs [old]`, limit 10: names == ["needle.txt"] and total_matched < 30 (today it counts the decoys). Also KindFilter::Folder finds `My Docs [old]/needle-dir`.
7. Helper: scope_glob("Tax Returns [2024]") == "Tax Returns [[]2024[]]/**" and scope_glob("a/b") == "a/b/**".

Headless UI test in tests/controls.rs next to `search_scope_button`, using tests/common/mod.rs:
- `Fixture::new("scope-special")`, then create `fx.path("drafts[old]")/todo.txt` containing `needle` before `Ui::open(cx, &fx.dir)`.
- Use a bracket name without a space: a small fixture only fails today for brackets, since whitespace scopes still work there through the post-filter.
- `ui.go_to(&fx.path("drafts[old]"))`, `ui.click("search-scope")`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query("needle".into(), true, cx))`, `ui.click("by-contents")`, then assert `ui.names() == ["todo.txt"]`.

Existing tests that must stay green: engine.rs `searches_a_folder` and `finds_apps_without_indexing_them`; tests/controls.rs `search_scope_button` and `scope_bar_controls`; tests/nu_module.rs `fff find notes --here`.
verifier.risks:
- Depends on fff-search 0.11.0 internals: an empty raw_query skips the literal fallback, and Constraint::Glob strings go verbatim to globset. Tests 2 and 3 pin both. If the project ever enables fff's zlob feature, bracket escaping must be re-checked (extglob and brace flags).
- Small ranking and semantics shifts in scoped name search, because raw_query no longer contains the scope: combo boost now applies, and a lone `dir/` becomes folders-only as it is unscoped. No existing test pins the old behaviour.
- The engine-side retry is a second grep pass; cap it to the remaining time budget or a no-hit search can take twice the limit.
- Scoped content search for a constraint-only pattern changes from returning nothing to a literal search inside the folder. That is intended, but it is user-visible.
- The exact starts_with post-filter must stay; non-UTF-8 folder names still cannot match (to_string_lossy), as today.
- Using PathSegment for all scopes, as originally proposed, would make ordinary scopes inexact wherever a folder name repeats deeper in the root; do not take that variant.
- The `*`, `?` and backslash folder-name tests must be unix-only, since those names are invalid on Windows.

orchestrator_notes: 'search-truncation-honesty' is on the trunk (read its done record and commit 40f8e86: content_search now asks for one line a file and limit + 1 files, and the engine fixes part of the folder-with-a-space case). Its reviewer left this for you: a contents search inside a folder with a space in its path can fill its page with hits outside the folder, which are then dropped, so the window says 'No Results' with '0+ items' while files in the folder do match (picture: /home/user/polish-tools/shots/search-truncation-honesty-review-folder-with-space-crowded.png). After your change that search must list the folder's matches: add it as a test. fff-search's literal fallback also gives a folder-scoped contents search that found nothing a second full time budget, so one search can run to nearly twice the limit.
